title: Kohl's drops Black Friday sale ad with doorbusters and $15 Kohl's Cash deal
summary: Kohl's has released its 64-page Black Friday ad four weeks early, detailing sales and doorbusters that will begin on Thanksgiving Day. Shoppers can earn $15 Kohl's Cash for every $50 spent, a higher rate than usual, with early deals available from November 1-3. The ad also highlights Black Friday week sales from November 25-29 and specific doorbuster deals for November 28-29.

title: Walmart offering alcohol pickup at stores in 29 states
summary: Walmart has expanded its alcohol pickup service to 2,000 stores across 29 states, allowing customers to purchase alcohol through Walmart Grocery Pickup. The service requires valid photo ID upon collection and will also include alcohol delivery in select California and Florida stores. This expansion is a strategic move to compete with other retailers offering similar services and to enhance e-commerce economics, despite local and state regulations.

title: What Has Been Driving Akamai Technologies’ Performance?
summary: Akamai Technologies (NASDAQ: AKAM) exceeded Q3 revenue and EPS expectations, primarily driven by strong growth in its security solutions business. This positive performance led to an upward revision of the company's guidance for Q4 and full-year 2019. The article highlights Akamai's shift from its core content delivery network (CDN) business, which faces competition from large internet players, towards leveraging its network reliability and insights to build a robust security business and become a key player in edge computing.

title: Shopify complaints mount from online retailers and consumers
summary: Online retailers and consumers are increasingly voicing complaints against Shopify, focusing on issues like chargebacks, abrupt account closures, and funds being held hostage. While Shopify provides a vital platform for numerous merchants, its rapid growth has led to accusations of heavy-handed practices regarding fees and dispute resolution. Despite an A+ rating from the BBB, the company faces scrutiny over its handling of customer and merchant conflicts and even rumors of potential class-action lawsuits.

title: UPS Debuts Home Delivery of CVS Medicine by Drone
summary: UPS has expanded its drone delivery services beyond hospital campuses, completing its first revenue-generating home deliveries of prescription medicines from a CVS Health Corp. pharmacy in Cary, N.C. The company used autonomous drones monitored by remote pilots, lowering packages by a winch, and plans to further grow drone deliveries, especially in rural areas, to compete with rivals like Amazon and FedEx. UPS was the first company approved by the FAA for commercial drone flights under the broadest airline rules.

title: Lineage Logistics | Success Story
summary: Lineage Logistics, a company revolutionizing temperature-controlled supply chain and logistics, moved its international headquarters from Irvine, California, to Michigan in 2017. The decision was driven by Michigan's talent pipeline, optimal location to customers, and support from the MEDC, despite competing sites in other states. Since relocating, Lineage Logistics has exceeded its initial job creation promises and significantly boosted its revenue, partly due to its strategic investment in Michigan.

title: How a Houston-area county landed a national retailer's 2M-square-foot, 1,300-job distribution center
summary: Ross Stores Inc. has selected Waller County in the Houston area for a new 2 million-square-foot distribution facility. This development is projected to create 1,300 full-time jobs, marking a significant economic boost for the region. The article details the successful move to attract this national retailer.

title: Calendar: Black Friday is Nov. 29. Target: Eh, close enough
summary: Target Corp. is set to launch a two-day Black Friday preview sale on November 8, three weeks ahead of the actual Black Friday. This move positions Target as the latest retailer to adjust its strategy amidst an unusually short holiday shopping season.

title: Expansion Planned at Culver City's Blackwelder Office Campus
summary: Kilroy Realty Corp. recently purchased the Blackwelder office complex in Culver City for $186 million with plans to significantly expand the existing 19-building, 158,000-square-foot campus. The property, currently fully leased with tenants paying below-market rates, is located in an area benefiting from the growth of content production companies like Amazon, Apple, and HBO.

title: Amazon Web Services Revenue by Year
summary: The article details the historical revenue growth of Amazon Web Services (AWS) from fiscal year 2014 to 2019, highlighting its increasing contribution to Amazon's overall revenue. AWS revenue reached an all-time high of $35.026 billion in 2019, representing 12.5% of Amazon's total revenue, demonstrating consistent strong year-over-year growth. It also provides background information on Amazon.com, Inc., including its founding, IPO, and key products.

title: Amazon Annual Revenue by Segment: FY 2001 - 2020
summary: This article analyzes Amazon's annual revenue by segment from FY 2001 to 2020, focusing on North America, International, and AWS. In 2019, Amazon's total revenue reached an all-time high of $280,522 million, with North America contributing over 60%. AWS revenue also saw significant growth, increasing by 36.5% year-over-year.

title: Amazon Annual Revenue by Products & Services Group
summary: The article analyzes Amazon's annual revenue by product and service groups from 2014 to 2019, highlighting the significant contributions of Online Stores (over half of total revenue) and the rapid growth in Third-Party Seller Services, Subscription Services, AWS, and "Other" services. It also notes a slight decline in Physical Stores revenue in 2019. The report provides detailed financial figures and growth rates for each segment, underscoring Amazon's diverse revenue streams and market leadership.

title: Amazon Annual Revenue By Region: FY 2013 to 2020
summary: This article analyzes Amazon's annual revenue by region from fiscal year 2013 to 2020, highlighting the United States as the largest market. In 2019, the US contributed over 69% of Amazon's total revenue, reaching $193,636 million. Germany, the UK, and Japan are identified as other significant markets for the e-commerce giant.

title: Amazon Annual Revenue from Products and Services
summary: The article details Amazon's annual revenue from products and services, highlighting significant growth. In 2019, Amazon reported its highest-ever annual revenue from products and services, reaching $160.4 billion and $120.1 billion respectively. The company's revenue milestones include crossing $50 billion in product sales in 2012 and exceeding $100 billion in products and $50 billion in services for the first time in 2017.

title: Walt Disney Company’s Investor Call Disney+ Highlights
summary: The Walt Disney Company's recent investor call highlighted details about Disney+, including its launch on Amazon, Samsung, and LG devices, and its European rollout on March 31st. Despite increased direct-to-consumer revenues, the segment operating loss grew due to Hulu consolidation and Disney+ launch costs. CEO Robert Iger also provided updates on the successful Disney+ trial in the Netherlands and mentioned FX content moving exclusively to Hulu.

title: JPMorgan Chase targets gig economy tech firms with e-wallet platform
summary: JPMorgan Chase has developed an e-wallet platform aimed at gig economy companies like Airbnb, Lyft, and Amazon, offering virtual bank accounts and perks to customers. This strategy allows JPMorgan to assume payment processing for these tech firms, addressing the threat of revenue loss to nonbanks and fintech companies. The bank aims to partner with the top 10 e-commerce and gig economy companies, simplifying refund processes and expediting payouts.

title: Google starts construction on $600M data center in unlikely burgeoning tech hub of New Albany, Ohio
summary: Google has begun construction on a $600 million data center in New Albany, Ohio, marking its third major tech facility in the area. The project is expected to be completed by early 2021 and follows investments from Facebook and Amazon, turning central Ohio into a data center hub due to significant tax cuts and strong electrical infrastructure. New Albany offered Google a substantial incentive package, including property tax abatement and waived fees, while the state of Ohio also provides sales tax exemptions for data centers.

title: Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph says company’s ‘secret weapon’ sets itself apart from Disney, other streaming services
summary: Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph believes the company's "focus" on streaming and movies is its "secret weapon" against new competitors like Disney+ and Apple TV+. Despite growing competition and concerns about Netflix's revenue stream, Randolph emphasizes the company's startup mentality and willingness to adapt, assuring its continued presence in the evolving digital streaming landscape.

title: Ralph Lauren offers consumers a DIY counterfeit-checking tool
summary: Ralph Lauren has launched Digital Product Identities, a DIY counterfeit-checking tool allowing consumers to verify product authenticity by scanning a label. This technology also provides product details and styling tips while offering Ralph Lauren real-time tracking and improved inventory management. The launch comes amidst increased attention on anti-counterfeiting technologies following reports of fake goods being sold on resale sites.

title: KKR makes formal approach to Walgreens Boots on record buyout
summary: KKR & Co. has formally approached Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc. regarding a potential deal to take the company private, which could represent the largest-ever leveraged buyout. The transaction faces challenges due to the large amount of financing required, with Walgreens Boots having a market value of about $56 billion and $16.8 billion in debt. This move would allow Walgreens Boots to adapt to a changing retail landscape away from public shareholder demands, especially with pressure from online competitors like Amazon.

title: Kroger launches auto buying program with TrueCar
summary: Kroger has partnered with TrueCar to launch the Kroger Auto Buying Program, offering customers access to pricing information, guaranteed savings on new cars, and discounts on used cars. This initiative is part of Kroger's strategy to provide more services and perks to its customers, mirroring efforts by competitors like Costco and Amazon, and contributes to its alternative profit portfolio which is projected to generate significant operating profit. The program is available to customers of several Kroger-owned grocery chains and aims to provide a more transparent car-buying experience.

title: Is this the peak of Amazon? 3 reasons why growth might be hard to come by
summary: This article explores whether Amazon's rapid growth phase might be peaking, citing three main red flags for investors. These include the increased costs associated with one-day shipping without commensurate profit growth, declining profitability and market share for Amazon Web Services (AWS), and a decrease in consumer preference for Amazon.com over competitors like Walmart.

title: Under the Hood of QRAFT AI Enhanced U.S. Large Cap ETF (QRFT)
summary: The QRAFT AI Enhanced U.S. Large Cap ETF (QRFT) is an actively managed ETF that uses a proprietary artificial intelligence system to select large-capitalization U.S. stocks. The fund aims for long-term capital appreciation by focusing on factors like quality, size, valuation, momentum, and low risk, with AI continuously learning optimal factor weights based on macroeconomic and valuation conditions. QRFT may serve as a large-cap equity allocation, offer factor exposure, or act as an alternative investment due to its cutting-edge technology.

title: Under the Hood of QRAFT AI Enhanced U.S. Large Cap ETF (QRFT)
summary: The article explores the QRAFT AI Enhanced U.S. Large Cap ETF (QRFT), highlighting its use of advanced AI and machine learning algorithms to select large-cap U.S. stocks. QRFT aims for long-term capital appreciation by dynamically optimizing factor weights across quality, size, valuation, momentum, and low risk, adapting to macroeconomic conditions. It is presented as a suitable option for investors seeking large-cap equity exposure, factor exposure, or an alternatives allocation based on cutting-edge technology.

title: REX Shares Rolls Out A New ETN For FAANG Fans
summary: REX Shares has introduced a new exchange-traded note (ETN) called FNGS, expanding its lineup of leveraged FANG+ products. This ETN is designed for investors seeking focused exposure to high-growth FAANG+ stocks like Facebook, Amazon, Apple, Netflix, Alphabet, Tesla, Nvidia, Alibaba, and Baidu. The FNGS ETN offers a more representative approach to large- and mega-cap technology investing compared to traditional tech ETFs that might be heavily weighted towards Apple and Microsoft but lack sufficient FAANG+ exposure.

title: Nike Pulling Its Products From Amazon in E-Commerce Pivot
summary: Nike Inc. is ending its pilot program to sell sneakers and apparel directly on Amazon's website, a move that follows the naming of a former EBay CEO as Nike's new chief. The athletic brand will cease direct sales on Amazon, which began in 2017, but will continue to utilize Amazon’s web services.

title: Elisa rolls-out industrial IoT to 100 P&G factories, says ‘world will change’ with 5G
summary: Finnish telecoms company Elisa is expanding its industrial IoT monitoring and insights solution to 100 Procter & Gamble factories, building on an initial rollout at 10 sites. Elisa emphasizes the transformative potential of 5G in industrial settings, beyond just speed, by enabling streaming analytics at the network edge. The company offers its data-analytics and digital-twinning recipe to third parties, leveraging its own successful internal digital transformation.

title: Target shoppers can tap the app and get groceries dropped on their porch the same day
summary: Target now offers same-day delivery through its app, allowing customers to order groceries and other items for a $9.99 fee, waived for purchases over $75 from Nov. 17-26. Shipt members receive free delivery, and new users can try a four-week free trial. This move positions Target competitively alongside other retailers like Walmart and Amazon, which also offer various same-day delivery options.

title: Why Costco Is Thriving Even as the U.S.-China Trade War Drags On
summary: Costco is successfully navigating the U.S.-China trade war despite tariffs that are impacting other retailers. The company benefits from its high sales volumes, fast inventory turnover, and a business model that relies on membership fees for a significant portion of its operating earnings, providing stability in a volatile retail sector. Costco's scale grants leverage with vendors, and its strategic expansion and focused inventory management allow it to maintain low prices and strong sales growth, outpacing competitors and the broader retail market.

title: Motorola Solutions Has Made $25 Million This Year Working with ICE and CBP
summary: Motorola Solutions has earned $25 million this year from contracts with ICE and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, providing radio communication services and software. This work has drawn scrutiny given ICE's controversial policies, including family separations and unsanitary detention conditions. The company's corporate responsibility statement emphasizes ethical operation and community support, yet they did not comment on their contracts with VICE.

title: ‘Not on Netflix’ and proud of it, Tubi boasts in ads
summary: Tubi, a free ad-supported streaming service, is launching a new advertising campaign that highlights its content not available on Netflix to attract viewers suffering from "subscription fatigue." The campaign, featuring actor Chris Noth, emphasizes Tubi's free model and its extensive library of movies and TV shows, including a "Not on Netflix" category. Despite some concerns about promoting competitors, Tubi aims to position itself as a complementary service to paid subscriptions.

title: Ubiquiti AmpliFi Alien Wi-Fi 6 router has a big, beautiful color touchscreen
summary: Ubiquiti has released the AmpliFi Alien Wi-Fi 6 router, featuring a large color touchscreen and a design reminiscent of an Amazon Echo. This router boasts 8x8 MIMO Wi-Fi 6 Technology for extended range and speed, supports mesh networking, and includes software features like simple setup and a free VPN service. It is priced at $379 and offers advanced performance optimizations for multiple connected devices.

title: PayPal just struck L.A.’s biggest ever tech deal
summary: PayPal Holdings Inc. announced the acquisition of Honey Science Corp. for $4 billion, marking the largest tech deal in Los Angeles history. Honey, a popular browser extension for price comparison, will be integrated into PayPal and Venmo to extend consumer engagement beyond checkout. This acquisition is seen as transformative, accelerating PayPal's capabilities and market relevance, especially given Honey's profitability and strong growth.

title: Chipotle Announces Alexa Reordering Skill By Giving Away Echo Dots To Rewards Members Named Alexa
summary: Chipotle has launched a new skill for Amazon Alexa, allowing customers to reorder their favorite meals for delivery or pickup. To celebrate this launch and reaching seven million Rewards Members, Chipotle is giving away Amazon Echo Dots to all existing Chipotle Rewards members named Alexa. This initiative is part of Chipotle's broader artificial intelligence strategy, which also includes AI-generated voice assistants in all 2,500 restaurants to streamline the ordering process.

title: Wingstop lets Twitch users order food while watching livestreams
summary: Wingstop has introduced a "Wing Calculator" Twitch Extension that allows users to order food directly while watching livestreams on the platform. This initiative, available through select streamers, aims to capture delivery orders from Twitch's engaged audience, predominantly millennial men who watch others play video games. The campaign highlights Twitch's Extension apps' flexibility for e-commerce, offering a new revenue stream beyond sponsorships and subscriptions.

title: What to look for in a TV on Black Friday?
summary: This article provides comprehensive advice on what to consider when buying a TV during Black Friday sales. It covers key factors such as screen size, resolution (4K vs. 8K), HDR technology, connectivity (HDMI ports), panel type (OLED vs. LCD), and smart TV features. The author also advises on distinguishing between genuine bargains and lower-quality brands.

title: Alexa can remind you to take your medication
summary: Amazon's Alexa has launched new features allowing select customers to set medication reminders and request prescription refills through voice commands, in partnership with Omnicell and Giant Eagle Pharmacy. This initiative aims to simplify medication management at home while prioritizing user privacy and security through voice profiles and personal passcodes. Amazon plans to expand these features to more pharmacies in the future, highlighting the ongoing innovation in voice technology for healthcare.

title: Movado Group struggles as watches become status symbols
summary: Movado Group reported a significant drop in earnings and sales, attributed to a failed marketing campaign and intensifying challenges in the watch market. This contrasts with the strong demand for high-end Swiss luxury watches, which continue to be prominent status symbols, especially in the U.S.

title: Synchrony says suspicious email blast citing Amazon didn't involve a data breach or fraudulent activity
summary: Synchrony Financial clarified that a suspicious email blast sent to customers, which cited Amazon, was due to an internal error and did not involve a data breach or fraudulent activity. Consumers are advised that they do not need to take any action. Amazon also acknowledged the issue, stating the notification was distributed by Synchrony in error.

title: Synchrony Bank apologizes for deposit email
summary: Synchrony Bank issued an apology after mistakenly sending out emails about a small deposit into "Amazon Credit Builder accounts" to people who were not their customers or even Amazon account holders. Many recipients believed the emails were a scam or indicated a data breach. The bank clarified it was an internal error, with a spokesperson from the Better Business Bureau suggesting the affiliation with PayPal might be how email addresses were acquired.

title: TCL 55" Class 6 Series 4K HDR Roku Smart TV (2019) Review
summary: The TCL 55R625 4K HDR Roku Smart TV (2019) offers excellent color accuracy, deep blacks, and an auto game mode, making it a strong contender in the midrange TV market. Despite a 60Hz native refresh rate, its overall performance, especially for gaming and HDR content, is impressive for its $600 price point. The Roku interface is highlighted as intuitive and fast, contributing to a top-tier user experience.

title: Amazon and eBay accused of selling cosmetics containing mercury
summary: Online marketplaces Amazon.com Inc. and eBay Inc. are facing accusations of selling skin-lightening products with high mercury levels, particularly as the holiday shopping season approaches. Activist groups tested 158 products sold on these platforms across 12 countries and found that 60% were contaminated with mercury, which was not listed as an ingredient. This situation highlights the product safety risks associated with the convenience of online shopping.

title: Black Friday Amazon deals' costs: Workers' health, climate change and your own taxes
summary: This article examines the hidden costs of Amazon's convenience, focusing on worker exploitation, environmental impact, and tax subsidies. It highlights the physical dangers faced by Amazon employees due to high-speed quotas, the company's significant carbon footprint, and the financial burden placed on taxpayers through subsidies, while also noting recent worker and activist pushback.
